media:group.media:title: 3D-Messsystem für den Industrieeinsatz
media:group.media:description: Überarbeitete Fassung (empfohlen) Fraunhofer IOF entwickelt ein neues 3D‑Sensornetzwerk für die Stahlteilfertigung. Im Verbundprojekt DIKUQ („Digitalisierung der kaltplastischen Umformung durch kontinuierliche Qualitätskontrolle“) setzen Forschende mehrerer Institutionen und Unternehmen im Werk des Projektkoordinators Ostseestaal GmbH & Co. KG teilautomatisierte Systeme um. Diese ermöglichen, Werkstücke entlang der gesamten Prozesskette zu erfassen und in Kooperation mit den Mitarbeitenden vor Ort zu bearbeiten. Das im Video vorgestellte 3D‑Messsystem kommt an einer Schiffbaupresse zum Einsatz. Dort erproben neben dem Fraunhofer IOF auch das Fraunhofer IGP, die Universität Rostock und die MSR‑Service GmbH Automatisierungstechnik. Das Besondere an diesem Projekt: Alle Systeme kooperieren miteinander, fügen sich nahtlos in bestehende Produktionsprozesse ein und bewähren sich unter den herausfordernden Arbeitsbedingungen eines Stahlwerks.

entry.title: Aircraft-to-ground quantum key distribution - lecture by Christopher Spiess | Photonics4Future

media:group.media:title: Aircraft-to-ground quantum key distribution - lecture by Christopher Spiess | Photonics4Future
media:group.media:description: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers secure sharing of secret keys backed by the laws of physics, particularly utilizing single photons. This presentation explores aircraft-to-ground entanglement-based QKD. It addresses the challenges typically faced in multi-platform QKD, such as channel loss, polarization alignment, synchronization issues and large background noise, while proposing innovative solutions. The seminar will also showcase the flight scenario in the QuNet-SE3 demonstration and its latest advancements in technology.

entry.title: Multimodal 3D measurement: imaging beyond 3D - lecture by Peter Kühmstedt | Photonics4Future

media:group.media:title: Multimodal 3D measurement: imaging beyond 3D - lecture by Peter Kühmstedt | Photonics4Future
media:group.media:description: At the Fraunhofer IOF’s Imaging and Sensing department, we develop customized systems and methods for optical imaging, sensing, image processing, and data handling. In our webinar, we will present some of our latest developments and highlight specific application examples. If you are looking for photonic solutions for documenting measurement objects, creating digital twins, obtaining input data for augmented reality applications, and numerous other use cases, you can look forward to gaining insights into our work and getting in touch with us.

entry.title: Characterization of Optical Surfaces and Coatings - lecture by Anne-Sophie Munser | Photonics4Future

media:group.media:title: Characterization of Optical Surfaces and Coatings - lecture by Anne-Sophie Munser | Photonics4Future
media:group.media:description: Comprehensive characterization throughout the photonic process chain is essential for high-performance optics. The webinar provides an overview of surface and coating characterization with a particular focus on roughness analysis using the PSD function and its connection to scattered light. Additionally, it addresses light scattering-based particle and defect detection as well as links to stray light analysis. These topics are highly relevant for aerospace, lithography, and optical metrology.

entry.title: Micro-optics for automotive lighting - lecture by Dmitrii Stefanidi | Photonics4Future

media:group.media:title: Micro-optics for automotive lighting - lecture by Dmitrii Stefanidi | Photonics4Future
media:group.media:description: New applications, new possibilities: The maskless design is the key to the future of automotive lighting. Developed by Fraunhofer IOF, this cutting-edge technology opens up innovative exterior design options for vehicle designers while keeping manufacturing costs low. In this lecture, Dmitrii Stefanidi discusses micro-optical system design. As the lead designer for car lighting systems at Fraunhofer IOF, he shares his expertise and insights on the topic.

entry.title: Metasurfaces and optical metasystems - lecture by Falk Eilenberger | Photonics4Future

media:group.media:title: Metasurfaces and optical metasystems - lecture by Falk Eilenberger | Photonics4Future
media:group.media:description: New applications, new possibilities: Metasurfaces are the optics of the future. These structures offer advanced functions extending far beyond classic optics. In this lecture, Falk Eilenberger will provide insights into metasurface development, explain the basics and provide a glimpse into the future of metasystens. Falk is the head of the Micro- and Nanooptics department at Fraunhofer IOF. The leading application-oriented research institute for photonics.

entry.title: New System for 3D shape measurement of transparent objects in 360 degrees - Glas360Dgree 3D Scanner

media:group.media:title: New System for 3D shape measurement of transparent objects in 360 degrees - Glas360Dgree 3D Scanner
media:group.media:description:
To scan glass, transparent, black or shiny objects, our new 3D scanner uses a new method that makes such uncooperative surfaces directly measurable in 3D. The 3D scanning system creates a sequential thermal fringe projection and uses the thermal radiation emitted from the surface of the objects themselves for 3D shape measurement.
Learn more about the Glass360Dgree system on our website https://www.iof.fraunhofer.de/en/pressrelease/2021/3d-mwir-en.html

media:group.media:title: Quantum computer ion addressing optics
media:group.media:description: A brief introduction to our prototype for an ion addressing optics. When fully built, it will be implemented in the ion trap quantum computer for Europe that is under development in the AQTION project.

entry.title: Quantum imaging technology – first quantum video taken

media:group.media:title: Quantum imaging technology – first quantum video taken
media:group.media:description:
Scientists at the Fraunhofer IOF have taken their first images using a novel quantum imaging technology. Using a so-called "single crystal set up", the scientists were able to generate quantum images and videos. This technology is particularly relevant for the field of life sciences, since it allows to image tissue with particularly high con-trast and information, while at the same time maintaining a low illumination dose.
We will build the next generation of microscopes, quantum microscopes.

entry.title: Joseph-von-Fraunhofer-Preis 2016: Revolution in der Beleuchtung: LED-Arrayprojektion

media:group.media:title: Joseph-von-Fraunhofer-Preis 2016: Revolution in der Beleuchtung: LED-Arrayprojektion
media:group.media:description:
In den vergangenen Jahren haben moderne Licht- und Projektionssysteme den Bereich von einfachen Beleuchtungen oder Präsentationen verlassen. Durch stetige Verbesserung der Leistung bei gleichzeitiger Reduktion des Bauraums erschließen solche Systeme neue, hochinteressante Anwendungsfelder in den Bereichen Allgemeinbeleuchtung, Automotive oder Mess- und Sicherheitstechnik.
Die Diplom-Physiker Dr. Peter Schreiber, Dr. Peter Dannberg und Marcel Sieler sind seit 2009 damit befasst, LED-Beleuchtungsmodule für verschiedenste Anwendungsgebiete weiterzuentwickeln. Mit der Neuentwicklung eines mikrooptischen Arrayprojektors – im Gegensatz zu bis dahin üblichen Einzelaperturlösungen – gelang es den Forschern, den Zusammenhang zwischen Baugröße der Systeme und Beleuchtungsstärke zu entkoppeln. Damit werden maßgeschneiderte Lichtlösungen mit ultradünnen Projektionssystemen möglich.

media:group.media:title: Mikrooptische Abbildungssysteme für den Consumermarkt
media:group.media:description: Facetvision´s optische Fabrikationstechnologien basieren auf parallelisierten Verfahren zur Erzeugung von mikrooptischen Komponenten. Das Ziel ist, Optik und Elektronik im Aufbau, der Funktion und der Fertigung zu verschmelzen. Ähnlich der Halbleiterindustrie werden im Gegensatz zu Einzelmustern Wafer für den Prozess der Parallelisierung genutzt, so dass eine hohe Zuverlässigkeit, Miniaturisierung und kostengünstige Produktion erreicht werden kann.
